newsitem.title: USA: Warm weather helps N.Dakota crops advance.
newsitem.headline: Warm weather helps N.Dakota crops advance.

text.p: Seasonably warm temperatures during the week ended Sunday helped advance the drying down and harvesting of North Dakota crops, according to the weekly state crop report.

Sugarbeets made the most progress, advancing to 88 percent complete, ahead of 39 last year and the average of 70 percent. Soybeans were 76 percent harvested versus 60 a year ago and the average of 73 percent.
Harvesting of corn for grain and sunflowers lagged average levels, but the report said harvesting of those crops was expected to get into full swing this week.
Corn harvest was 10 percent finished versus 31 a year ago and the average of 33 percent. Sunflowers were 18 percent harvested, versus 32 last year and the 28 average.
Soil moisture ratings fell from levels seen during the previous week and the previous year but still remained above average.
Pasture and range condition was rated 38 percent good to excellent, a slight decline from 39 percent at that level last week.
